connection_condition: superhero.publisher_id references publisher.id; each superhero carries at most one publisher
description: A superhero is published by a publishing imprint; the connection is a direct identifier reference but a publisher is an independent entity, not a part of the superhero.
A superhero has one recorded gender category drawn from an independent vocabulary.
A superhero has one recorded moral alignment, which is what distinguishes heroes from villains.
A superhero has one recorded racial origin drawn from an independent vocabulary.
A superhero has one recorded skin colour drawn from the shared colour vocabulary.
A superhero has one recorded eye colour drawn from the shared colour vocabulary.
Skin colour is a colour role: its recorded values are a subset of the shared colour vocabulary and are drawn from the same value domain.
Eye colour is a colour role: its recorded values are a subset of the shared colour vocabulary and include 'No Colour'.

connection_condition: hero_power.hero_id references superhero.id and hero_power.power_id references superpower.id
description: A superhero possesses zero or more superpowers and a superpower may be possessed by many superheroes; the relation is many-to-many and neither side depends on the other for existence.
A superhero is composed of its attribute ratings: a rating row carries no meaning without the superhero it rates and is removed together with that superhero.
A rating measures exactly one named super attribute; the attribute is an independent vocabulary entry.
Each rating carries exactly one numeric attribute value; the value is interpretable only in combination with its attribute.

connection_condition: superhero.id, hero_attribute.hero_id and hero_power.hero_id share the same value domain; no link row references a missing superhero
description: The superhero identifier appears under a different column name in the link tables; both name the same identifier concept and can be used interchangeably when joining.
Both are labels of the same superhero row: superhero_name is the published codename and full_name the real-world name, which is frequently unrecorded.

connection_condition: publisher.id identifies the record whose publisher_name carries the label
description: The publisher identifier and the publisher name refer to the same publishing entity; questions may ask for either the name or the identifier.
The gender ratio is derived from the superhero count taken separately for each gender: the male count divided by the female count.
The maximum attribute value for a named attribute is derived as the largest attribute value recorded under that attribute.
The minimum attribute value for a named attribute is derived as the smallest attribute value recorded under that attribute.
The average weight is derived as the arithmetic mean of the recorded weights within the stated population of superheroes.
The superhero count is derived by counting the distinct superheroes that satisfy the stated condition.
